items.briefing:
Be cautious with calendar invitations right now. Researchers at Barracuda have identified a phishing technique where attackers send malicious .ics calendar files — the kind used by Outlook and Google Calendar — to trick people into clicking harmful links. These can arrive looking like legitimate meeting requests, making them easy to accidentally accept.

In other news, DXC Technology and Primary have launched a new AI-powered security service aimed at Australian organisations, which may be worth exploring if your RTO is reviewing its security posture.

**Practical tip:** Before accepting any unexpected calendar invite, verify the sender through a separate channel before clicking any links inside it.

featured.title: Barracuda warns calendar invites are being used for phishing via .ics files
featured.quote: Calendar invites exploited for phishing poses immediate threat to Australian organisations using email systems.
